samples.summary: Unrequested scope: the PR flips the Yorkie auth-webhook posture to enforce-by-default and adds a whole new backend identity (`yorkie-service` token) inside a change whose issue (#1044, `docs/tasks/active/20260907-notes-share-toolbar-todo.md`) is "mount the notes toolbar on the share-link route". The task doc's scope list (N1–N8 + divider + docs) contains none of this, no task doc exists for the flip, and it reverses the rollout the canonical design doc had specified (`docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md` step 2 was "Shadow mode (default)"; the goal is "Safe, reversible rollout (shadow/log-only before enforcing)"). Cost is outside the codebase: any existing deployment that has already registered the webhook methods with the variable unset flips from allow-all to denying on the next deploy — exactly the "deploy sequencing" hazard the same doc warns about (`docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:297`) — and it drags along backend service tokens, three ops scripts, `YorkieService`, and the template gate. Whether or not enforce-by-default is right, it is a separate posture change that deserves its own change and its own rollout note, not a rider on a frontend toolbar fix.
samples.evidence: isYorkieAuthEnforced: `raw?.trim().toLowerCase() !== 'false'` — unset now enforces; the notes-share-toolbar todo/lessons docs never mention the webhook.

samples.summary: Design-doc discipline: the change flips the meaning of `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` but updates only `docs/design/notes/notes.md` and `docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md`. Other canonical docs still assert the old default and are now wrong about a security boundary: `docs/design/sharing.md:208-213` ("This is **off by default**. `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` is unset in a stock deployment, which puts the controller in shadow mode"), `docs/design/revision-history.md:504-508`, `docs/design/template-gallery.md:669`, `docs/design/docs/docs-image-editing.md:300`, and the index line `docs/design/README.md:155` ("shadow→enforce rollout"). The repo files docs by validity and folds corrections into the canonical subsystem doc; leaving four docs stating the opposite default is the parallel-truth failure that discipline exists to prevent.
samples.evidence: sharing.md:208 "This is **off by default**. ... puts the controller in shadow mode"

samples.summary: Internal contradiction inside the doc this change does update: after redefining enforcement as the default (line 29) and shadow as opt-in (line 217), the Risks section still prescribes "watch the shadow logs ... before flipping `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true`" (279-281), and line 251 still mitigates with a "staged shadow→enforce rollout", and line 260 with "acceptable for the shadow phase ... before enabling enforcement at scale" — a phase that no longer exists by default. A reader following the read-only-viewer verb mitigation is told to do something the new semantics make impossible (setting `true` is now indistinguishable from unset).
samples.evidence: line 279-281 'shadow mode is exactly the instrument for this — ... before flipping YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true' alongside line 29 'Enforcement itself is the **default**'

samples.summary: Comments added by this very change state the pre-change default and so contradict it: `packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:447` ("the Yorkie auth webhook ships in shadow (allow-all) mode by default and so may not refuse the write either") and `packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts:64` ("the webhook allows everything until a deployment both registers its methods and sets `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true`"). The same PR's design doc goes out of its way to record the shadow-default claim as wrong, then re-asserts it in new code.
samples.evidence: new editor.ts hunk: 'the Yorkie auth webhook ships in shadow (allow-all) mode by default'

samples.summary: The sibling wrapper the new one is modelled on keeps the rationale this change declares false: `packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:40` still says the webhook "ships in shadow mode by default ... so with the default configuration this flag is the write boundary", and `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:4413` and `packages/docs/test/view/editor-read-only.test.ts:381` say the same. The correction was applied to the notes copy only, so the two guards now document opposite deployment assumptions for the identical mechanism.
samples.evidence: docs/src/store/read-only.ts:40 'ships in shadow mode by default (`YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE`)'

samples.summary: Duplication of a security-relevant wrapper: `packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts` is a near-verbatim reimplementation of `packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts` — same reader-allowlist argument, same memoization map, same `get`/`set`/`defineProperty`/`deleteProperty`/`getPrototypeOf`/`setPrototypeOf`/`preventExtensions`/`has`/`getOwnPropertyDescriptor`/`ownKeys` traps, largely the same prose. The store-shaped part is genuinely per-package (store unification is a stated Non-Goal in `docs/design/shared-core-extraction.md:46-48`), but the trap machinery is store-agnostic and could have been one `readOnlyProxy(target, readers)` helper. The copies have already diverged (notes adds the idempotency `WeakSet` and the `undo`/`redo` null handling; docs has neither), so the same question now has two answers and the next fix has to be made twice.
samples.evidence: identical trap set and comment structure across the two files; notes adds READ_ONLY_VIEWS/HISTORY_METHODS that docs lacks

samples.summary: Wrong layer / missed reuse for token minting: `AuthService` is the canonical minter of Yorkie auth-webhook tokens (`issueYorkieUserToken` / `issueYorkieShareToken`, reading `JWT_SECRET` and `YORKIE_TOKEN_EXPIRES_IN` once, `auth.service.ts:68-87`), and it also owns verification. The new module instead constructs its own module-level `new JwtService()` and the secret/expiry are re-read in three more places (`YorkieService` constructor, `yorkieServiceTokenInjectorFromEnv` off `process.env`, plus each script), each with its own `'10m'` fallback and its own missing-secret posture (AuthService throws via `requireConfig`, these warn). A third `issueYorkieServiceToken()` on `AuthService` plus a thin env helper for the DI-free scripts would keep one owner of the yorkie-token shape.
samples.evidence: yorkie-service-token.ts: `const jwt = new JwtService();` and duplicate `?? '10m'` fallbacks vs auth.service.ts:68

samples.summary: One environment variable now has two official readings: `isYorkieAuthEnforced` treats unset as enforcing, while `assertYorkieAuthEnforced` and `scripts`/`register-templates.ts` require the literal `'true'`. Both are documented as deliberate, but the result is that a stock deployment is simultaneously "enforcing" (webhook) and "not enforcing" (gallery gate), which is the divergence a single variable invites. If the intent is "operator affirms the Yorkie methods are registered", that is a different question and deserves its own variable name rather than a stricter reading of this one.

The extraction reintroduces the import the deleted comment existed to avoid: `shared-document.tsx` previously refused to import `notes-settings` because Rollup would hoist it (and the notes engine) into a shared chunk past the size gate. `shared-notes-layout.tsx` imports `notes-settings` and `NotesView` statically and is imported only by `shared-document.tsx`, so it folds back into that chunk. The lessons doc records the measurement (225 chunks, under the cap), so the gate is fine — but neither the design doc nor the code records why the old constraint no longer applies where the old comment used to be.
samples.evidence: deleted comment in shared-document.tsx: 'Passing it from here would mean importing notes-settings into this route too, which makes Rollup hoist it'

verdict.reason: Verified independently. (1) The code is present as quoted: `isYorkieAuthEnforced` at packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts:20-22 returns `raw?.trim().toLowerCase() !== 'false'`, and its docblock (lines 5-18) states enforcing is the default and shadow is an explicit opt-in. (2) The new backend identity exists: packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-service-token.ts, consumed by yorkie.service.ts, template/seed/register-templates.ts, template-review.ts and three packages/backend/scripts/*.ts. (3) The flip belongs to the change under review, not to prior history: .agent-review/correctness/summary.md:3 and .agent-review/docs/summary.md:3 both describe reviewing the enforce-by-default flip and the new yorkie-service token path alongside the issue #1044 notes-toolbar work. (4) The scope claim holds: docs/tasks/active/20260907-notes-share-toolbar-todo.md (scope N1-N8 + divider + docs) and the paired lessons doc never mention the webhook, enforcement, or service tokens, and no active task doc covers the posture flip. (5) The prior posture really was shadow-by-default, corroborated by still-current docs that this change did not reconcile: docs/tasks/active/20260902-template-gallery-public-tier-todo.md:251 ("default shadow mode"), docs/tasks/active/20260902-revision-history-todo.md:32-40, docs/tasks/active/20260905-release-v0.6.9-todo.md:79-83 (ENFORCE=true still framed as an outstanding deployment step), and packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts:63-67. The design doc still lists "Safe, reversible rollout (shadow/log-only before enforcing)" as a Goal (docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:43) while lines 29-32 and 221-223 now declare enforce the default, and the deploy-sequencing hazard is the doc's own risk (line 297). No guard makes the flip unreachable (the auth controller and the public-template gate both consult the helper), and unrequested scope with an out-of-codebase deployment consequence is squarely in the design-fit lane's major band. Nothing here refutes the finding.
